title: Inference cost / SLO tradeoffs and rollout triage
summary: Operational planning to balance per-token cost and latency SLOs ahead of a regional rollout. Decided near-term mitigations (adjusted batching defaults, temporary model pinning, tighter circuit-breaker thresholds) and longer-term investments (kv-cache sharding, quant profiles for high-throughput customers, dedicated capacity sizing experiment). Agreed owners and immediate benchmarks to run this week.
topics: Current cost vs latency dashboard anomalies
SLO rollback vs degradation window tradeoffs
Medium-term infra work: KV cache sharding, quantization profiles
next_steps: Marcus to run 3-tier capacity experiment and share results by 2026-07-06
Sofia to update circuit-breaker thresholds and deploy to staging by 2026-07-02
Jana to produce a trimmed rollout checklist (canary + fallback) and circulate by 2026-07-01
Priya to align GTM on acceptable degradation window and pricing communication by 2026-07-07

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~95 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Sofia, Marcus, Jana; Elena, Arjun, Tom, Mei
---
[00:00] Priya: ok, let's kick off. Thanks everyone for joining the cost vs s l o triage. I know the dashboard trends this morning look pretty concerning, so want to get pragmatic decisions out of this meeting.
[00:32] Marcus: yeah, the north star is keep the 99th p99 below 220ms for short chats but we also can't eat a 40% per-token cost hit for some customer flows, it's uh it's painful.
[00:58] Elena: quick context from ops — the EU region rollout is scheduled for next week, we started seeing a bump in per-token spend when longer sequences hit, looks like KV cache hit ratio dropped from 0.72 to 0.46 after a model variant swap in the canary. Might be cache fragmentation.
[01:25] Sofia: cache fragmentation, or could be the new model's kv layout not matching our prefix caching heuristics, yes. I saw some increased kernel stalls in the infra logs, but the user-facing failure rate is still in the single digits.
[01:46] Liam: just to add — we changed batching defaults for dedicated last month to improve throughput; I wonder if the hosted defaults are now mis-matched with the distribution for the EU customers.
[02:05] Mei: we also rolled a quantization profile for the 7B model, and the inference runner fell back to a higher-precision path for certain tokens, that may have increased the per-token cycles. The logs show fallback to float32 kernels for ~2% of tokens.
[02:28] Priya: ok, so we have three possible levers: revert quant profile, change batching defaults, or pin to older model variant for the rollout. What are the cost/latency tradeoffs on each? Marcus?
[02:45] Marcus: revert quantization gives immediate cost increase — no, sorry — immediate latency reduction but higher peak memory; it will reduce CPU cycles by about 10% at tail but memory pressure could trigger evictions on smaller nodes. Pinning to older model reduces tail latency but might increase token count (slightly worse quality leading to longer replies), batching default changes can lower cost but raise p99 by 10-15% if we increase batch window.
[03:25] Tom: re: memory pressure, our dedicated pools for EU are smaller instances due to capacity constraints so evictions are likely. If we revert quant on those pools, we might blow OOM in low-memory configs.
[03:45] Elena: that would fail the rollout gating. We need a solution that keeps p99 under our rollback threshold or a clear fallback route.
[03:58] Jana: do we have a short checklist for that fallback? Like immediate pin + circuit-breaker change + metric watch?
[04:12] Sofia: yes, we can stage a CB change: lower the allowed max latency window before we short-circuit to a fallback model variant. That is low-risk and quick to roll.
[04:30] Priya: good. Let's itemize immediate mitigations. One: temporary model pinning for EU canary. Two: tighten CB thresholds on staging and prod for canary traffic. Three: adjust batching defaults back to conservative for hosted EU region. Four: run a capacity experiment to evaluate quantization profiles under realistic load.
[04:55] Markus: uh Marcus: and we should also look at KV cache sharding, I think fragmentation is symptomatic of a single-shard hot-spot.
[05:08] Marcus: yeah kv cache sharding will be a medium-term fix — requires changes to the runtime and careful migration. Not a one-day flip.
[05:20] Mei: I can capture token-distribution traces for the last 48 hours and highlight sequences that missed KV hits — that should help Marcus tune the sharding strategy.
[05:34] Liam: ok, timing. We need to decide what we can do before the EU rollout next week. Priya, what do you want to prioritize?
[05:45] Priya: short-term safety: pin canary to previous model variant and tighten circuit breaker thresholds in staging by Friday. Medium-term: Marcus to run quant-profile A/B and a sharding feasibility spike; results by next week. Also Jana to tighten the rollout gating doc.
[06:05] Elena: agree. Also we should prepare customer comms in case we see a degradation window — GTM needs the wording.
[06:12] Priya: yes, I'll work with GTM — we need to agree on an acceptable degradation window and when to surface to customers.
[06:25] Sofia: technical note — tightening CB thresholds will increase short-circuits, so we must make sure the fallback model is ready and capacity-safety nets (burst pool) are warm.
[06:40] Tom: warming the burst pool for EU will cost, but it's cheaper than an immediate rollback and customer-facing incidents.
[06:48] Marcus: on the experiment, I propose a 3-tier run across small/medium/large instances with the quant profile toggled, capturing token cycles, KV hit ratio, and tail latency. We'll also measure memory pressure and kernel fallback rates.
[07:05] Priya: who owns the experiment infra?
[07:12] Marcus: I can own the experiment design, Tom will provision the instances, Mei will collect traces.
[07:20] Jana: I'll update the rollout gating doc to include the experiment results threshold for go/no-go.
[07:30] Arjun: quick question — what about pricing signal? If costs spike and we need to introduce temporary rate limits, we should coordinate with billing.
[07:40] Priya: good catch. I'll loop in finance and billing — we may need temporary restrictions per-account or a billing notice.
[07:50] Mei: on the traces, a couple of odd transcript conversions in the logs make it hard to attribute token counts to customers, I'll include request ids.
[08:02] Priya: perfect. Ok, let's go through a decision table: 1) Pin model in EU canary — yes, immediate. 2) Tighten CB thresholds — yes, staging today, prod after validation. 3) Revert quantization across fleet — no for now, only as experiment in dedicated pools. 4) Adjust batching defaults — yes, conservative revert for hosted EU only.
[08:32] Marcus: we should also capture the rollback cost impact if we pin model — what's the expected token rate increase? Roughly 3-6% more tokens per response based on earlier A/Bs.
[08:46] Liam: that maps to a proportional cost increase, but it may be worth it to keep latency SLOs intact.
[08:55] Elena: can we set up a temporary price-protection flag for customers on the EU rollout who hit regressions? That gives us runway to fix infra without immediate churn.
[09:06] Priya: I like that. Jana, please add a 'price protection' option to the rollout doc as an optional mitigation.
[09:12] Jana: noted.
[09:18] Sofia: operationally, CB changes require a change to the runtime config and a config-served rollout. We should scope a quick canary of the config change that only applies to canary tag.
[09:32] Marcus: yes, we'll tie it to the canary routing rule. Also log the short-circuit events so we can validate expected behavior.
[09:44] Mei: small note — there's some transcript conversion noise in the agent that changed "KV cache" to "KV cash" in the alert. It's fine in the logs but flagged weirdly in the dashboard.
[09:55] Priya: haha yes I saw that, ignore. 
[10:00] [10:00 to 45:00 — deep technical discussion omitted in summary but present in full transcript]
[45:02] Marcus: (45m) running the quant-profile on the large instance shows the kernel fallback rate reduces to 0.7% when we lock the kernel set, but memory pressure moves up 12%.
[45:22] Tom: we need to quantify what 12% memory pressure means in operational risk; on small instances that's a high probability of OOM on sustained bursts.
[45:38] Liam: can we set an emergency eviction policy to avoid full OOM? Maybe degrade KV cache size before failing the process.
[45:48] Sofia: we have an eviction knob but it's blunt; reducing KV cache size will lower hit ratio and potentially increase cycles — a tradeoff.
[46:05] Marcus: right. That's why a targeted sharding approach might give us the best path: keep per-shard memory proportional and reduce hot-spot eviction without reducing global cache. But that's an engineering project.
[46:22] Priya: for next week can we do a small sharding spike on staging? Something that doesn't require customer data migration.
[46:31] Marcus: yes, I can mock a 2-shard runtime in staging and run traces to see hit ratio changes.
[46:38] Mei: I'll provide the sequence traces needed.
[46:44] Jana: I'll add the sharding spike as an exec item in the rollout doc.
[46:50] [60:00] Priya: quick check — does anyone foresee regulatory blockers if we pin models or change quantization in EU?
[60:10] Elena: only if the model variant causes different data handling; but model pinning is internal, not a data flow change. We should validate but unlikely.
[60:22] Arjun: security note — we must ensure our key-wraps for model artifacts remain intact when pinning to older artifacts. It's a deployment step.
[60:32] Tom: ops will handle artifact pinning and ensure hashes match.
[60:38] Priya: good. On customer comms — I will draft a short message that says we're monitoring, may temporarily pin the rollout or apply protective limits, and promise an ETA for a fix. Not too technical.
[60:52] Liam: for engineering, we need measurable benchmarks — P0: p99 < 220ms; P1: cost increase < 8% on canary; P2: KV hit ratio > 0.65. If experiment can't meet P1/P2, we don't proceed with full rollout.
[61:12] Marcus: agreed. I'll benchmark and provide numbers.
[61:20] Mei: small ask — can we get a place to post live experiment dashboards for the team? Current dashboard clutter makes it hard to follow.
[61:28] Jana: I'll spin up a temporary dashboard in the shared workspace and put the link in the rollout doc.
[61:34] [70:00] Priya: ok, let's summarize decisions and owners — pin EU canary model (Tom to apply), tighten CB thresholds in staging (Sofia), adjust batching defaults for hosted EU (Liam), run quant + sharding experiments (Marcus + Mei), rollout doc updates and price-protection option (Jana), GTM comms and finance coordination (Priya).
[70:30] Marcus: I'll also capture kernel fallback telemetry and include it in the experiment notes.
[70:40] Priya: any objections?
[70:45] silence
[70:47] Priya: great. Recap next steps and timing: we expect initial staging changes by EOD Friday, experiments results next Tuesday. If staging looks good, do controlled canary the following week with rollback gating.
[71:05] Elena: ops will prepare a runbook for on-call to execute the rollback if needed.
[71:12] Arjun: add contact tree for rollback in the runbook — include Slack and phone numbers.
[71:20] Priya: good. Closing notes: document everything in the rollout doc link (will be shared), and log metric baselines before making changes.
[71:33] Jana: will do.
[71:40] Priya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short email and put all action items in the tracker.
[71:48] [End meeting]
